newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mostly down.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Monday after an article in the Futures Daily said copper futures would maintain a downward trend in the mid to long-term due to oversupply, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 23,450 yuan ($2,826) per tonne, losing 30 yuan. It opened at 23,500 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,390 and a high of 23,550.
April fell 10 to 23,320, May 40 to 23,310, June, the only rising contract, put on 10 to 23,400, August dropped 50 to 23,450, September 60 to 23,450 and October 500 to 23,450.
Combined volume fell sharply to 40,550 tonnes from 93,850.
Copper opened mixed and then fell. Short-covering later pushed prices off their lows but they still ended down from Friday's close.
Traders said the Futures Daily report hurt the confidence of long position holders but there was no panic selling seen.
"The article made investors afraid of heavy selling by hedgers," one trader said. "But panic selling did not emerge because of speculative buying at lower levels."
Aluminium ended down. April fell 150 to 15,600 yuan per tonne, May 260 to 15,690, June 200 to 15,950 and July 150 to 16,150.
Combined volume rose to 3,880 tonnes from 3,410.
